disputes.reply: Hi lee, thanks for raising this. We compared the delivered file city_timelapse_09.mp4 (seconds 0.0–3.25) with a video in the public Vript dataset (source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2VCg3df0ZnI, around seconds 96–99). The delivered frames do not show a city timelapse or a view from a window. They show an indoor studio set: a person in a rainbow wig and yellow shirt and a person in a hat and tutu in front of a blue wall with a 'Looney Tunes' poster. The same scene, with the same people, poses, props and poster, appears in the matched video at 97.6 s and 98.7 s. The first match frame at 96.5 s is a wider shot of the same set, so the alignment is offset by about a second, but the footage is clearly the same. Because the delivered content is this studio scene and not the timelapse you describe, your statement about filming it does not cover this file. The finding stays on hold, and the payment for this clip (0.14) is not released. If you uploaded the wrong file by mistake, please deliver your original timelapse as a new submission so it can be reviewed separately.
